core_meaning.short_meaning: Divinely protected, sheltered by God; famed early scholar Mu'adhah al-Adawiyyah.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Muadhah (مُعَاذَة) is an Arabic feminine given name meaning 'she who is granted divine refuge', 'protected by God', or 'safeguarded from harm'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Mu'adhah bint Abdillah al-Adawiyyah, the illustrious female scholar, ascetic, and senior hadith narrator who studied directly under Aisha and Ali ibn Abi Talib.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Placed under divine sanctuary and refuge (isti'ādhah), preserved by Allah from spiritual and worldly tribulations.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root ʿ-w-dh is the basis of seeking refuge in God from all evil (as in Surah al-Falaq and Surah an-Nas). Mu'adhah al-Adawiyyah of Basra was revered as one of the most brilliant and pious women in the early Islamic generation (Tabi'at). Her narrations are accepted in the six canonical collections (al-Kutub al-Sittah) including Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

faq.a: Muadhah (مُعَاذَة) is an Arabic feminine given name meaning 'she who is granted divine refuge', 'protected by God', or 'safeguarded from harm'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Mu'adhah bint Abdillah al-Adawiyyah, the illustrious female scholar, ascetic, and senior hadith narrator who studied directly under Aisha and Ali ibn Abi Talib.

faq.q: What is the origin of Muadhah?
faq.a: The root ʿ-w-dh is the basis of seeking refuge in God from all evil (as in Surah al-Falaq and Surah an-Nas). Mu'adhah al-Adawiyyah of Basra was revered as one of the most brilliant and pious women in the early Islamic generation (Tabi'at). Her narrations are accepted in the six canonical collections (al-Kutub al-Sittah) including Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
Yes. The recorded language/origin is Arabic; the source form is مُعَاذَة.

faq.q: How is Muadhah written in Arabic?

faq.a: It is not claimed as a Qur'anic personal name. The personal name Muadhah is not in the Qur'an; its triliteral root ʿ-w-dh forms the foundation of the sacred Qur'anic refuge formula (e.g. 113:1, 114:1).

Venerated in Islamic scholarship as an unimpeachable hadith transmitter whose rulings shaped Islamic legal understanding of women's worship. Named after Mu'adhah al-Adawiyyah, whose inquisitive scholarly questioning of Aisha clarified essential rulings on prayer and fasting for all Muslim generations.
An approximate romanized guide is moo-AA-dhah. Initial 'moo', followed by pharyngeal 'ʿayn' and long vowel 'aa', ending with soft interdental 'dhah'.

faq.q: Is Muadhah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The documented naming sources record Muadhah as a female name; actual use can vary by language and community.
